blocks.text: For years, multi-step routines, impulse beauty purchases, and a tolerance for skin peeling or irritation were seen as necessary tradeoffs for anti-aging results. Driven by the long-held “Tiis-Ganda” belief, dermatological actives like retinol emerged as category standards. Today, a subtle yet distinct cultural shift is reshaping how women in their late 20s and early 30s are approaching skincare, as consumers increasingly trade high-maintenance, irritating anti-aging products for gentle, barrier-first alternatives. While retinol remains widely prescribed for reducing signs of aging and keeping the skin supple and youthful, its side effects frequently pose challenges for those with sensitive skin.
